records.title: Agentic Much? Adoption of Coding Agents on GitHub
records.reason: Superseded version; retain for transparent numerical-drift audit, not a separately included independent study.

study_extract.design: Authors' GitHub repository-mining estimate reported in the v1 abstract; no independent full-methods replication.
study_extract.population: 129,134 projects according to official 2026-01-26 v1 arXiv abstract.
study_extract.outcome: Abstract reports 15.85%-22.60% estimated coding-agent adoption, a version-specific observational estimate.
study_extract.limitations: Trace detection and selection frame are not independently rechecked; v1 is a version of the same study, not a new replication.

records.title: Agentic Much? Adoption of Coding Agents on GitHub
records.reason: Retained as accepted-manuscript precursor; journal version is preferred for main bibliography.

study_extract.design: Authors' revised GitHub repository-mining estimate in the 2026-04-08 v2 abstract.
study_extract.population: 128,018 projects according to the arXiv v2 abstract.
study_extract.limitations: Not an independent replication of v1 or of the later ACM version; no human review of complete methods or denominator reconciliation here.

records.title: Agentic Much? Adoption of Coding Agents on GitHub

study_extract.design: Peer-reviewed observational mining of public GitHub coding-agent traces; journal accepted 2026-05-13, online accepted-manuscript 2026-06-26.
study_extract.population: 128,018 projects as reported by ACM article abstract, sampled according to its trace-based study method.
study_extract.outcome: Authors report 22.20%-28.66% estimated coding-agent adoption by 2026-02-21; this is not all-GitHub population prevalence or causal productivity.
study_extract.limitations: Trace sensitivity/specificity, project frame and missing silent-agent use require method-level review; journal and arXiv revisions count as ONE scientific study.

records.title: The SPACE of Developer Productivity: There's more to it than you think.

study_extract.design: ACM Queue conceptual multi-dimensional developer-productivity framework, published 2021-03-06.
study_extract.population: Methodological framework and practice examples; not an experimental sample that estimates agent outcomes.
study_extract.outcome: Defines satisfaction/well-being, performance, activity, communication/collaboration, efficiency/flow as distinct productivity dimensions.
study_extract.limitations: Framework alone demonstrates no measured benefit from coding agents and supplies no causal or carbon effect.
